tag: Episode 7 · The Festival Where the Sun Stopped
title: The Festival Where the Sun Stopped

beats.t: At sunset, even the smells of the festival street were noisy. Browning sugar, charring skewers, laughter mingled with drumbeats.
Yeongnyangi. I've decided. I'm spending the rest of my life on this island.
We arrived less than an hour ago.
An hour is enough. They fry clouds here. If this isn't heaven, what is?
Half a fried cloud was wedged between Yeoni's hooves. The drumming child had split it for them. Steam still rose from it.
The first bite deserves reverence. Star rating after I swallow.
It's hot. Blow on it first.
Don't worry. Pigs handle hot food well. ...Probably.
Song packed the street. A noodle shop sang while tapping pots with ladles. A rice-cake shop improvised songs from customers' names.
Nobody sang well. Everybody sang loudly.
That man's completely off-key, and the customers love it even more.
On this island, that is the right rhythm.
Yeoni opened their mouth wide. At that moment, a bell rang from the highest stage at the street's far end. Dong.
The drums stopped midbeat. Songs, laughter, even the crackle of frying oil—all at once.
...What? Who pressed Mute?
The sun, half-submerged at the horizon, had stopped. Neither setting nor rising. A red semicircle pinned to the sky like a frozen screen.
The sun has stopped.
The sun isn't something that stops.
Look there.
One black feather stood embedded at the top of the highest stage. The very feather they had seen falling over the river.
Crows poured down beneath it. Hundreds settled on every rooftop. Not one cawed.
Hear this announcement.
A large crow in black judicial robes stood beside the feather. A white mask, neither smiling nor weeping, covered its face.
From this moment, singing is forbidden on this island. So are rhythm, whistling, and loud laughter.
Offending mouths will be stamped. That is all.
A singing ban in the middle of a festival? What's the festival supposed to run on? A minute of silence?
Lower your voice. Those crows are all ears.
If singing's banned, what about humming?
Singing.
Clapping?
Rhythm.
Then breathing? Breath has rhythm too.
Breathing is still allowed. For now.
One by one, people closed their mouths. They put down ladles and hid drumsticks in their sleeves. Nobody asked why.
Only the skewer seller could not hold back. A customer dropping a skewer apparently struck him as funny. Ha, ha, ha.
A crow dived. Its beak struck the back of his hand, leaving a gray stamp.
He was only laughing!
The seller opened his mouth to laugh again. Ha, ha. Instead of sound, only air came out. Less air than before.
Each stamp diminishes the voice. Expression is the energy that brings what is inside outward. Words, songs, flavors you create.
Block the mouth and all three are blocked together.
All three? Taste too?
Yeoni looked down at the fried cloud between their hooves. The sparkling sugar coating had turned ash-gray.
Yeoni bit into it. Chewed. Chewed again.
...There's no taste.
When the sun stops, fire cools. That sun cooks the flavors of this island.
This is a crime. You fry a cloud, then take away its flavor? That's fraud, a crime, an international incident.
This is not a nation.
Then it's a cosmic incident. I'm review-bombing this entire island.
Perhaps the injustice was too much. A sound burst from Yeoni's nose.
OIIIIIINK!
The entire street turned toward Yeoni. Hundreds of rooftop crows cocked their heads at the same moment.
That sound had pitch.
No, that wasn't singing! It was a pig noise!
The final note rose. Singing.
A black shadow brushed Yeoni's hoof. A sting. A coin-sized gray stamp marked the pink skin.
My hoof! My cute little hoof's been branded!
This child came from another island. You can't stamp them before even explaining the rules here.
The masked crow looked down at Yeongnyangi. No eyes were visible through the mask's holes.
Set foot on this island and its ears hear you. Make your excuses at trial. Starting with the next stamp.
Judicial robes fluttered. The crow vanished toward the feather. The other crows remained motionless on the rooftops.
...Yeongnyangi. Is my voice smaller now?
Your voice sounds fine. Nothing to worry about yet.
Knowing that's supposed to comfort me makes it sadder.
Behind the festival street lay a night market. Or what had once been one. The awnings remained, but their colors had drained away. Skewers, candy, people's faces—all gray.
It's even quieter here than on that street.
These people were stamped earlier. The feather had been eating away at this island long before the sun stopped.
Two or three gray stamps marked the backs of the merchants' hands. When customers came, they pointed at prices instead of speaking.
An old woman at a candy stall saw Yeoni's hoof and beckoned them closer.
Hello. I'm not a scary pig. It's my first time here.
The woman spoke with breath instead of voice. Like air escaping a balloon.
One takes laughter, two take song, three take speech. There were three stamps on her hand.
You... can't speak anymore.
She shook her head, then placed one candy in Yeoni's hoof. A gray candy.
Thank you. I'll enjoy it even if it has no taste. I mean, I'll enjoy it.
The woman's eyes crinkled in a smile. A silent smile. Yeoni could not believe anyone could put a stamp on that.
Yeoni put the candy in their mouth. It tasted of nothing. Still, they rolled it around until it was gone.
Yeongnyangi. What did this island used to be like?
It was midday all day. The festival began at noon, and the sun set only when the songs ended.
That sun is Byeong, the light of high noon. It must reach noon again before this island can have another day.
Then we just push the sun back up to noon, right?
Easy to say.
Talking's always easy. It's the talking island. ...Oh, right, currently the no-talking island.
A drum rolled out from the far side of the market. Someone had dropped it. Boom. The sound rang far too loudly.
The crows on the roofs spread their wings together. The drum's owner had already hidden behind an awning. Yeoni picked up the drum and froze.
...Oh. I didn't play it. Seriously.
Put it down. Slowly.
Yeoni lowered the drum gently. The crows tilted their heads, then folded their wings again.
This isn't an island. It's a library. With about a hundred librarians.
Hundreds.
Thanks for the correction. Not thankful at all.
Yeoni walked among gray awnings. Their hunger grew with every step. Food was everywhere, yet there was nothing they wanted to eat.
This is the scariest part. Being hungry but wanting none of the food.
That is how people wither. First they lose flavor, then laughter.
Then everyone on this island is withering right now.
That is why we must not stay long. You have a stamp too.
No way. I haven't tasted a single specialty yet. I'm not leaving before the flavor comes back.
Motivated by appetite.
Appetite is noble. Humanity discovered fire because it was hungry.
You are currently a pig.
Pigs are noble too!
Then another scent slipped among the gray smells. Simmering soy sauce, toasting sesame, and the faintest hint of something burned.
Wait. Yeongnyangi. Did you smell that?
What?
Something delicious! Actually delicious! A smell that isn't gray!
Yeoni's nose moved on its own. Their hooves followed it. Yeongnyangi had no chance to stop them.
Yeoni. Don't just follow it.
My nose went first. I'm only following my nose.
The scent led to a narrow alley at the market's end. Sunlight never reached it. Only lamps under the eaves were lit.
Deep inside came the crackle of frying oil. And a very small voice.
It was not a song. Too fast for a song, too rhythmic for ordinary speech.
Turn up the heat, oil the pot. Mute the mouth, but flavor won't stop. Gray sky overhead, my pan burns red.
...Is that rap? On this island? Right now?
If discovered, that won't end with just three stamps.
A brown otter crouched in a ramshackle food cart at the alley's end. Turning rice-cake skewers over a small pan, the otter muttered so softly that only the pan could hear.
The rice-cake skewers glowed orange. In the middle of the gray island, they alone had color.
...An ember.
That fire was not borrowed from the sun. It was kindled within.
Yeoni took a step without realizing it. A gray plate broke underfoot. Clink.
The otter jumped. The skewer in its paw flew into the air. Yeoni caught it in their mouth.
Hey. That's my skewer.
...Delicious.
Of course it is. I grilled it. But what are you? A pig?
Five stars. No, six.
Stars only go up to five, you flower-headed pig.
And why is a flower-headed pig sniffing around someone else's alley?
The smell spoke to me first. Said it was delicious.
So this is an island where otters rap.
Not rap. A recipe recital. Just happened to have a beat.
People call a recipe with a beat rap.
People are wrong.
Wingbeats poured overhead. The alley entrance darkened. Crows were descending toward the sound.
You saw it. All of it. Heard the rap too.
Ah, I heard nothing. My ears were folded.
If you heard it, you're an accomplice. Run, pig.
